# Homarr Card URLs: Path-Only Hrefs for Multi-Hostname Access

## Problem Frame

After `halos-core-containers` PRs #122 (multi-hostname Traefik) and #123 (`${fqdn}` / `${domain}` tokens), a HaLOS device answers on multiple hostnames simultaneously: mDNS (`<host>.local`), DHCP-DNS bare/short, DHCP domain (`<host>.<dhcp-domain>`), VPN-routed FQDNs, and raw IPs. TLS, Authelia cookies, and OIDC redirect URIs all adapt per-hostname.

**Homarr cards do not.** Cards generated by `homarr-container-adapter` bake `https://<host>.local/<path>` at registration time (`homarr-container-adapter/src/registry.rs:174-189`, `src/signalk.rs:103-107`). A user reaching the dashboard via VPN or DHCP-DNS hostname and clicking a card is jumped back to `.local`, which won't resolve in their context. This defeats the motivating use case of #122.

The fix is to store **path-only hrefs** (`/cockpit/`, `/grafana/`, `/signalk-server/...`). The browser resolves them against the current origin natively at click time — exactly the mechanism HTML defines for relative URLs.

### Why this works in Homarr's existing architecture

Homarr already treats "what is my origin" as a per-request property: `homarr/packages/common/src/url.ts:7-23` exposes `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders(headers)` which returns `${proto}://${host}` from `x-forwarded-proto` + `x-forwarded-host`, and `packages/auth/redirect.ts` uses this to construct OIDC redirect URIs per-request. Multi-hostname-aware code already exists in the project; this brainstorm extends the same pattern to app card hrefs and to server-side fallback resolution of those hrefs.

### What changes

1. **`appHrefSchema` accepts path-only hrefs** in addition to absolute URLs.
2. **The `pingUrl ?? href` fallback gains a request-aware path-only branch** for upstream correctness: when `pingUrl` is unset and `href` is path-only, expand against `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders` if request headers are available, else fall back to a configured internal base or `null`. **In the HaLOS deployment this branch is rarely hit** because the adapter explicitly sets `pingUrl` on every internal app — the resolver short-circuits at step 1. The path-only-fallback branch matters for upstream Homarr users who hand-edit apps without setting pingUrl. Behavior for absolute hrefs is byte-identical to today.
3. **The adapter writes path-only hrefs** for internally-routed apps and continues to set `pingUrl` explicitly using the same internal base it uses today (`http://host.docker.internal:80<path>`). External links stay absolute. The user-facing href becomes hostname-agnostic; the internal pingUrl is unchanged in shape.
4. **App cards already use plain `<a>` (verified).** `homarr/packages/widgets/src/app/component.tsx:147-161` renders `AppLink` as Mantine's `UnstyledButton` with `component="a"`, producing a plain HTML anchor with `target="_blank" rel="noreferrer"` (when openInNewTab). No Next.js `<Link>` is used in the widgets or boards packages. Path-only hrefs work via standard browser navigation against the current origin. **No change needed to navigation primitive.**

### What does NOT change

- The `pingUrl ?? href` fallback semantics for absolute hrefs (every Homarr deployment today): byte-identical.
- Homarr's URL invariant: every value the schema accepts is still a meaningful URL (absolute, OR a relative reference per RFC 3986 §4.2 — both are standard web concepts).
- Authelia/OIDC/Traefik configuration: unchanged from PRs #122/#123.

## Requirements

### Homarr fork (`hatlabs/homarr`)

- R1. **Relax `appHrefSchema`** in `packages/validation/src/app.ts` to accept path-only hrefs (`^/[^/]`) in addition to absolute `scheme://...` URLs. Implementation must restructure (likely `z.union` of an absolute-URL validator and a path-only validator) since `z.string().url()` rejects path-only strings outright. The existing `javascript:` rejection and the empty-string-to-null transform must be preserved on both branches; the path-only branch must reject protocol-relative (`//host/...`) and any leading character other than a single `/` followed by a non-`/`.

- R2. **Evolve the `pingUrl ?? href` fallback into a request-aware resolver.** Introduce `resolveServerUrl(app, headers?)` returning the absolute URL that server-side code should use to reach the app, or `null` when none can be derived. Resolution order:
    1. If `app.pingUrl` is set, return it. (Byte-identical to today for any app with `pingUrl`.)
    2. Else if `app.href` is absolute, return it. (Byte-identical to today for any app with absolute href.)
    3. Else if `app.href` is path-only AND `headers` were supplied: return `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders(headers) + app.href`.
    4. Else if `app.href` is path-only AND a `HOMARR_INTERNAL_BASE` env var is configured: return `HOMARR_INTERNAL_BASE + app.href`.
    5. Else: return `null`.
  Every existing `pingUrl ?? href` call site reads through this helper. Known call sites: `packages/api/src/router/widgets/app.ts:32,73` (ping widget — has request context, gets per-request expansion); `packages/request-handler/src/lib/cached-request-integration-job-handler.ts:97` (background job — no request context, gets `HOMARR_INTERNAL_BASE` or null). For absolute-href apps, every call site behaves identically to today. For path-only-href apps, the resolver yields a usable absolute URL when headers are available (the common case for user-initiated server-side work) and falls back to env-configured base for genuinely-detached jobs.

- R3. **Bookmarks widget: render the path in place of the hostname for path-only entries.** The widget at `packages/widgets/src/bookmarks/component.tsx:235,282` currently renders `new URL(app.href).hostname` as a per-bookmark sub-label so users can distinguish bookmarks that point to different services. With path-only hrefs, every internal bookmark would render the same hostname (the user's current origin) — useless as a disambiguator, and `new URL(app.href).hostname` itself throws `TypeError: Invalid URL` for path-only inputs, crashing the widget's React subtree. Reframe the field: treat the sub-label as "where this bookmark goes," not "what host it points to." For absolute hrefs, keep rendering the hostname (today's behavior — byte-identical). For path-only hrefs, render the path (e.g., `/cockpit/` → `/cockpit`, trailing slash trimmed). The path *is* the disambiguator for path-routed services. Implementation: try/catch around `new URL(...)`; on parse failure, render `app.href` directly (with trailing slash trimmed for cosmetic consistency). Two-line change, one file, no behavior impact on absolute hrefs.

- R4. **No navigation-primitive change required.** Verified during this brainstorm: `homarr/packages/widgets/src/app/component.tsx:147-161` (`AppLink`) already renders as a plain HTML `<a>` via Mantine's `UnstyledButton` `component="a"`. Browser handles path-only hrefs natively. Retained as a requirement only to document the verification and to gate against any future change that would introduce `<Link>` for app cards (which would silently break path-only navigation by intercepting clicks into Next.js's client-side router).

- R5. **Audit for other consumers** beyond R2 and R3. Search scope: tRPC routers in `packages/api/src/router/`, integration middleware, request-handler jobs, server components, UI link constructors. Each finding classified as "navigation-only (relax)" or "server-internal (route through `resolveServerUrl`)" and handled accordingly. Quantify the diff size (files touched by null-branch propagation) before drafting the upstream PR (submission gated by the External Communication Policy).

- R6. **Authoring as upstreamable PR** against `homarr-labs/homarr`. PR framing: "Allow path-only navigation hrefs for self-hosted multi-hostname / reverse-proxy deployments." Lean on the precedent that Homarr already handles multi-hostname per-request for OIDC (R2 reuses `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders`, the same primitive). Acceptance tests:
    1. Existing absolute-href apps behave identically (regression on ping widget + integration paths + bookmarks widget hostname rendering).
    2. Path-only hrefs accepted by schema; `javascript:` and protocol-relative still rejected.
    3. `resolveServerUrl` returns the per-request absolute URL when headers are supplied with a path-only href.
    4. Background-job consumer correctly falls back to `HOMARR_INTERNAL_BASE` (or `null` when unset).
    5. Bookmarks widget renders the path (trailing-slash-trimmed) in the sub-label position for path-only-href bookmarks, and continues to render the hostname for absolute-href bookmarks.

  > ⚠️ R6 is governed by the **External Communication Policy** above. The patch is prepared in the `hatlabs/homarr` fork; the upstream issue/PR/comments are drafted, presented for review, and submitted only after explicit approval — per artifact, per submission, including any post-submission edits.

### Adapter (`halos-org/homarr-container-adapter`)

- R7. **Replace the absolute-URL check** at `src/registry.rs:274` with "path-only OR absolute URL" validation: accepts strings starting with a single `/` followed by non-`/`, preserves the existing absolute-URL parse, rejects malformed inputs in both branches, rejects protocol-relative `//host/...`. Document the accepted forms in the module-level rustdoc.

- R8. **Adapter still sets `pingUrl` explicitly** for internal apps (path-only and absolute alike), exactly as today. `pingUrl` is and always was an internal-network URL; it's not affected by the user-facing href change. The only adapter-internal refactor is in `derive_ping_url` (`src/homarr.rs:169`): today it calls `Url::parse(app.url)` and swaps the host with `host.docker.internal`; for path-only `app.url` there is no host to swap, so the function builds `http://host.docker.internal:80<path>` directly from the path. Absolute-href entries (external links) keep the existing host-substitution path. Per-app `ping_url` override in webapps.d remains supported and unchanged.

- R9. **Signal K dynamic discovery** (`src/signalk.rs:103-107`) emits path-only URLs of the form `/signalk-server/<package>/`. The Signal K-specific ping URL builder (`build_ping_url` at `signalk.rs:113`) already produces an internal URL (`http://host.docker.internal:3000<location>`); behavior unchanged. `build_icon_url` keeps emitting absolute icon URLs (icons load same-origin via the browser; multi-hostname is not a concern; Homarr's icon field accepts both forms; path-only icons would be cosmetic-only and skipped to keep diff minimal).

### Registry data (`halos-cockpit-config`, future webapps.d producers)

- R10. **Update `halos-cockpit-config/etc/halos/webapps.d/cockpit.toml`** to use `url = "/cockpit/"`. The file is a Debian conffile; on upgrade, dpkg uses standard conffile-update semantics. Existing devices with admin-edited cockpit.toml will see a prompt or default-keep behavior; **R11 (adapter-side migration) is the safety net** that reconciles stored Homarr cards regardless of whether the registry source is updated.

- R11. **Adapter-side migration** for existing devices. On first sync after upgrade, the adapter detects stored Homarr cards whose href is `https://<self-host>/<path>` matching a path-only registry entry, and rewrites the stored href in place to the path-only form. **Self-hostname source:** read `/etc/halos/hostnames.conf` directly (the public contract introduced by halos-core-containers PR #122) and apply the same `${hostname}` / `${fqdn}` / `${domain}` token-expansion semantics as `lib-hostnames.sh`. Match rule (tightened per review): rewrite only when (host matches an expanded entry, case-insensitive) AND (path equals the registry path) AND (scheme is https with no explicit port). Anything else — manually-edited port, scheme, path, or host pointing elsewhere — is treated as admin override and left untouched. **Pre-#122 fallback:** if `/etc/halos/hostnames.conf` is absent, fall back to `gethostname() + .local`.

- R12. **External-link entries** (`type.external = true`, e.g., docs.halos.fi cards) remain absolute URLs. Document the distinction in `halos-cockpit-config/AGENTS.md` or the adapter's README.

## Success Criteria

- A HaLOS device with `${hostname}.local` and a VPN FQDN (e.g., `halosdev.example.com`) in `/etc/halos/hostnames.conf` shows working cards under both. Clicking Cockpit from `halos.local` lands on `https://halos.local/cockpit/`; clicking Cockpit from `halosdev.example.com` lands on `https://halosdev.example.com/cockpit/`.
- After the first adapter sync following an upgrade, no duplicate apps appear in the Homarr DB; existing absolute-URL cards have been rewritten in place to path-only form, except for admin-edited cards which remain untouched.
- External-link cards still navigate to their absolute targets.
- Homarr's UI shows no validation error when an admin manually creates an app with a path-only href.
- The ping widget on a HaLOS-shipped card produces a valid health check using the adapter-emitted `pingUrl` (unchanged in shape from today's behavior; `derive_ping_url` builds the internal URL directly from the path for path-only entries).
- Upstream Homarr PR is open and reviewable (after explicit approval per the External Communication Policy).

## External Communication Policy

**Every interaction with `homarr-labs/homarr` (a third-party open-source project) requires explicit human approval before submission.** This includes, without exception:

- Opening issues
- Opening pull requests
- Editing existing issue/PR titles, descriptions, or bodies
- Posting comments or replies (including responses to maintainer feedback)
- Adding/removing labels, requesting reviews, requesting changes
- Closing issues or PRs

The implementing agent's workflow on any such action is: (a) prepare the artifact (code, draft issue text, draft PR description, draft reply), (b) present it in the conversation for human review, (c) wait for explicit go-ahead, (d) submit only after approval. Approval for one action does not transfer to subsequent actions — each external write requires its own confirmation.

This policy applies wherever the document references the upstream Homarr project, in any section. Internal HaLOS-org and hatlabs-org repositories follow the project's general AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md rules for PR/issue creation and are not covered by this section.

## Scope Boundaries

- Out of scope: ping URL / health-check logic beyond what R2 (server-side resolver, upstream-correctness) and R8 (adapter `derive_ping_url` builds path-only internal URL directly) require.
- Out of scope: any changes to Authelia / OIDC / Traefik (already handled by halos-core-containers PRs #122/#123). Interaction analysis is a Deferred-to-Planning research item, not a config change.
- Out of scope: Homarr's integration framework internals (Sonarr/Radarr/Nextcloud upstream URL storage). Integrations consume `resolveServerUrl` through the same fallback chain as today; their internals are unchanged.
- Out of scope: cross-origin SSO / shared sessions across hostnames.
- Out of scope: converting Signal K icon URLs to path-only (R9). Same-origin browser loading makes this code-cleanliness only.
- Out of scope: protocol-relative (`//host/...`) hrefs — explicitly rejected by R1.
- Out of scope: a `/usr/share/halos/webapps.d/` convention for package-shipped registry defaults. The conffile concern that motivated it earlier in this brainstorm is mitigated by R11 (adapter-side migration). If a future need for non-conffile package defaults arises, brainstorm it separately.

## Key Decisions

- **Option D (path-only href + server-side expansion via `resolveServerUrl`)** chosen over Option C (absolute href with `__halos_self__` sentinel + render-time token rewrite). Rationale: D extends standard web link semantics (path-relative resolution against current origin is foundational HTML), reuses Homarr's existing per-request hostname awareness (`extractBaseUrlFromHeaders`, already used for OIDC), and avoids introducing a private Homarr-specific convention. C is conservative against upstream rejection (no schema change) but invents a new abstraction the project doesn't have today; user judgment is that C's "magic host token" is a curve ball.

- **Engage upstream PR-first, with the concrete implementation in hand.** Rather than filing an exploratory issue, the upstream conversation happens on a real PR: the patch is prepared in the `hatlabs/homarr` fork, the PR is drafted against `homarr-labs/homarr`, and discussion with maintainers happens there with code to look at. Rationale: a concrete diff is more productive to discuss than abstract framing — maintainers can see the surface area, the test coverage, and the exact semantic change immediately, and any pushback is grounded in real code rather than hypothetical. HaLOS-side adapter/registry/migration work proceeds in parallel and ships regardless of upstream outcome (R11 adapter-side rewrite is what makes this work on a HaLOS device). PR submission, edits, and reply drafts are all gated by the External Communication Policy above.

- **Path-only, not protocol-relative.** `//host/...` would also satisfy multi-hostname but invents a host placeholder problem. Path-only is the simpler, more conventional answer for same-origin links.

- **Keep `external = true` cards absolute.** External links genuinely point elsewhere and have no equivalence to a current-origin path.

- **Adapter-side migration (R11) is the load-bearing ship guarantee, not the registry-data update (R10).** R10 changes the source of truth for new devices; R11 reconciles existing devices' stored cards regardless of conffile-prompt outcome. The success criterion ("no duplicates after upgrade") rests on R11, not R10.

## Dependencies / Assumptions

- Assumes `halos-core-containers` PRs #122/#123 (multi-hostname Traefik, `${fqdn}`/`${domain}` tokens) are merged and deployed (they are).
- Assumes Homarr's `extractBaseUrlFromHeaders(headers)` works correctly behind Traefik (forwarded headers populated). This is already exercised by the OIDC redirect path; behavior is established.
- Assumes app-card render path runs in a context with request headers available (Next.js server component / page route handler). Verified during R5 audit.
- Assumes `halos-marine-containers` registry entries follow the same `webapps.d` mechanism. **Unverified** — see Outstanding Questions.

## Outstanding Questions

### Resolve Before Planning

(All resolved during this brainstorm; see Verifications below.)

### Verifications (resolved 2026-04-28)

- **`host.docker.internal:80<path>` ping path works empirically.** Probe from inside the Homarr container on `halosdev.local`: Traefik:80 returns `301` → `https://host.docker.internal/cockpit/`, which fails TLS verification under default settings due to SAN mismatch but resolves correctly with `--no-check-certificate` (302 → `https://host.docker.internal:9090/` → 200 from Cockpit). Homarr's ping widget on `halosdev.local` reports correct status for HaLOS-shipped cards today — confirming Homarr's ping client tolerates the TLS-cert-mismatched redirect chain (likely accepts invalid certs for ping probes). R8's path-only branch produces the same `http://host.docker.internal:80<path>` URL via `derive_ping_url`, so it inherits the same working behavior. **R8 ships unchanged. No Traefik or ping-client work needed in this brainstorm's scope.**
- **Full webapps.d footprint is one file: `halos-cockpit-config/etc/halos/webapps.d/cockpit.toml`.** Workspace grep across all HaLOS package repos found no other producers. The `halos-homarr-branding` repo uses `/etc/halos-homarr-branding/branding.toml` (different path, different purpose — branding config, not registry entries). R10 scope is final: one file.

### Deferred to Planning

- [Affects R5][Implementation] Run the full audit of `app.href` consumers across Homarr. Quantify the file count for null-branch propagation. If the resolver-call-site count exceeds ~10 or several involve threading optionality through generic helpers, reconsider whether a separate `navigationHref` field upstream is a smaller diff than evolving the existing fallback.
- [Affects R8][Verify] Walk through the ping path under Authelia. The adapter-emitted `pingUrl` (`http://host.docker.internal:80<path>`) hits Traefik on port 80, which forwards to Authelia ForwardAuth. With no session cookie (background ping context), Authelia returns 302 to login, which Homarr's ping client likely interprets as "up" (got a response) but not in the way an app-availability check is meant to read. Verify what today's pingUrl actually returns under Authelia for absolute-href apps; the path-only-href case inherits whatever that behavior is. If it's broken, fix is shared with the R8 verify question above.
- [Affects R11][Technical] Verify Homarr's `app.selectable` tRPC endpoint (or alternative read path) returns the stored `href` so the adapter can detect equivalence at sync time. If not, R11 needs a different read mechanism (likely `board.getBoardByName` or similar).
- [Affects R11][Edge-case] Hostname-list parsing edge cases beyond "file present" / "file absent": empty file, malformed lines (FALLBACK mode in `lib-hostnames.sh`), soft-dropped `${fqdn}` lines when no DHCP domain resolves, hostname-rename history on long-lived pre-#122 devices. Decide whether the adapter re-implements `lib-hostnames.sh` semantics in Rust or shells out to the existing bash loader. Re-implementation must reproduce the loader's diagnostic signatures (`HALOS_HOSTNAMES_FALLBACK`, `HALOS_HOSTNAMES_SKIP`).
- [Affects R6][Process] Draft the upstream PR text (title, summary, motivation, test-coverage notes, code excerpts) for `homarr-labs/homarr`, present for human review alongside the prepared patch, and submit only after explicit approval per the External Communication Policy. No exploratory issue is filed first — the PR is the conversation surface. Capture maintainer feedback in the planning doc as it arrives.
